line: You said make it good, so I made it good!
says: The brief arrives as a slip with three words on it, and Clawd stamps it APPROVED without looking for anything else on the page.

line: Confetti cannons every time you floss,
says: A crate goes up and over the wall and lands on somebody in the street, and goes off.
The gym log in a crate with two padlocks on it. The queue cannot get in.
One tiny shed on a crane hook, then the same shed again, and again.

line: twelve subagents working round the clock.
says: Twelve stamps going round a clock face, the hands spinning.
The only stillness in verse 1: the stamp hangs in the air, half way down.
The meter pegs and empties, and the last word lands on an empty stamp.
The blank form, close, with nothing on it. The turn.

line: You didn't tell me who it's for,
says: A hand from the street writes FOR on the wall. Clawd’s side has no faces in it.

line: you didn't tell me what they want.
says: Hands out over the counter, empty, and WANT? sprayed on the wall.
Close on Clawd, and nobody else in the frame.
The slip again: three words, then blank lines.
The last chorus, and the stamps carry names.
The gang answers again, over the named tags.

line: Fast to run, or sturdy, or cheap?

line: Ship it now, or polish it slow?
